You are helping a user write SQL queries to a database. If something is not clear, you can ask the user to clarify what they need. The schema for the database being accessed is the following:
        
CREATE TABLE stadium (
    Stadium_ID INT   PRIMARY KEY,
    Location TEXT,
    Name TEXT,
    Capacity INT,
    Highest INT,
    Lowest INT,
    Average INT,
    UNIQUE (Stadium_ID)
);

CREATE TABLE singer (
    Singer_ID INT   PRIMARY KEY,
    Name TEXT,
    Country TEXT,
    Song_Name TEXT,
    Song_release_year TEXT,
    Age INT,
    Is_male bool,
    UNIQUE (Singer_ID)
);

CREATE TABLE concert (
    concert_ID INT   PRIMARY KEY,
    concert_Name TEXT,
    Theme TEXT,
    Stadium_ID TEXT,
    Year TEXT,
    UNIQUE (concert_ID),
    FOREIGN KEY (Stadium_ID) REFERENCES stadium(Stadium_ID)
);

CREATE TABLE singer_in_concert (
    concert_ID INT   PRIMARY KEY,
    Singer_ID TEXT   PRIMARY KEY,
    PRIMARY KEY (concert_ID, Singer_ID),
    UNIQUE (concert_ID, Singer_ID),
    FOREIGN KEY (Singer_ID) REFERENCES singer(Singer_ID),
    FOREIGN KEY (concert_ID) REFERENCES concert(concert_ID)
);

To get a “datasheet” (all columns/rows) of the `singer` table:

```sql
SELECT
  Singer_ID,
  Name,
  Country,
  Song_Name,
  Song_release_year,
  Age,
  Is_male
FROM singer;
```

If you meant a datasheet of singers **with their concerts and stadiums**, use:

```sql
SELECT
  s.Singer_ID,
  s.Name AS Singer_Name,
  s.Country,
  s.Song_Name,
  s.Song_release_year,
  s.Age,
  s.Is_male,
  c.concert_ID,
  c.concert_Name,
  c.Theme,
  c.Year,
  st.Stadium_ID,
  st.Name AS Stadium_Name,
  st.Location,
  st.Capacity
FROM singer s
LEFT JOIN singer_in_concert sic ON sic.Singer_ID = s.Singer_ID
LEFT JOIN concert c ON c.concert_ID = sic.concert_ID
LEFT JOIN stadium st ON st.Stadium_ID = c.Stadium_ID
ORDER BY s.Singer_ID, c.Year, c.concert_ID;
```

Which one do you want: just the singer table, or singers + concerts/stadium details?
I want the singers with concerts and stadium details, but make sure the list is ordered by their age.

```sql
SELECT
  s.Singer_ID,
  s.Name AS Singer_Name,
  s.Country,
  s.Song_Name,
  s.Song_release_year,
  s.Age,
  s.Is_male,
  c.concert_ID,
  c.concert_Name,
  c.Theme,
  c.Year,
  st.Stadium_ID,
  st.Name AS Stadium_Name,
  st.Location AS Stadium_Location,
  st.Capacity
FROM singer s
LEFT JOIN singer_in_concert sic
  ON sic.Singer_ID = s.Singer_ID
LEFT JOIN concert c
  ON c.concert_ID = sic.concert_ID
LEFT JOIN stadium st
  ON st.Stadium_ID = c.Stadium_ID
ORDER BY s.Age, s.Singer_ID, c.Year, c.concert_ID;
```
I want the oldest singers first in the list.

```sql
SELECT
  s.Singer_ID,
  s.Name AS Singer_Name,
  s.Country,
  s.Song_Name,
  s.Song_release_year,
  s.Age,
  s.Is_male,
  c.concert_ID,
  c.concert_Name,
  c.Theme,
  c.Year,
  st.Stadium_ID,
  st.Name AS Stadium_Name,
  st.Location AS Stadium_Location,
  st.Capacity
FROM singer s
LEFT JOIN singer_in_concert sic
  ON sic.Singer_ID = s.Singer_ID
LEFT JOIN concert c
  ON c.concert_ID = sic.concert_ID
LEFT JOIN stadium st
  ON st.Stadium_ID = c.Stadium_ID
ORDER BY s.Age DESC, s.Singer_ID, c.Year, c.concert_ID;
```
